currentContext.business: Kaya Limited operates a dermatologist-led network of skin, hair and body care clinics in India, combining clinical expertise with globally approved technologies and scientifically backed procedures to deliver personalised treatments. Alongside in-clinic services such as anti-ageing, acne and scars, brightening and pigmentation, laser hair reduction, hair care and body contouring, the Company sells a range of dermatologist-formulated skincare, haircare, bath-and-body and nutraceutical products that extend clinical benefits into daily consumer routines. Its in-house dermatologists design and formulate all services and products, and the business is supported by technology-enabled diagnostics, standardised treatment protocols and a customer-centric, doctor-first operating philosophy.

Launched in FY26: Kaya Firmup Essence Cellulite Control Cream
Kaya Skin Renew Sunserum with Capsule Technology
Kaya Soothe & Restore Post Treatment Balm
Kaya Ultra Glow Sunserum with Capsule Technology

currentContext.strategies: Strengthen the omnichannel ecosystem across clinics and digital channels, making expert dermatology more accessible, personalised and seamless|Deepen investments in cutting-edge dermatology technologies and digital healthcare solutions, including advanced diagnostics, skin analysis and treatment planning|Expand the clinic network across high-potential markets, alongside strategic relocations and infrastructure upgrades of existing clinics|Accelerate innovation across products, services and customer engagement platforms, with launches spanning hair care, anti-ageing, nutraceuticals, sun care and post-treatment recovery|Deploy advanced dermatological technologies across the network - additions during FY26 included Aerolase, MCT for Hair and Artiqa - to widen the specialised treatment portfolio|Reinforce a doctor-first, science-backed brand positioning through targeted digital campaigns, hyperlocal outreach, dermatologist-led education and lifestyle partnerships|Strengthen digital customer engagement and appointment management - automated reminders, follow-ups and visit confirmations - to reduce no-shows and improve service continuity|Invest in capability building, continuous learning and leadership development for dermatologists, therapists and clinic teams|The Board did not recommend any dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2026. Equity was raised during the year through a preferential issue of 20,90,068 equity shares to Axana Estates LLP on August 12, 2025, leaving paid-up equity capital of 1,51,87,609 shares of `10 each as on March 31, 2026. A transfer was made to general reserve from the share options outstanding account. The Company accepted no public deposits during the year and reported no one-time settlement with banks or financial institutions, no proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, and no change in the nature of its business operations. Employee incentives are delivered through the Kaya ESOP 2016 and Kaya ESOP 2021 plans, the latter amended during the year to permit the grant of Restricted Stock Units.
currentContext.expansion: Kaya's expansion is footprint- and technology-led rather than plant-based: the Company operates a network of 120+ dermatologists, 80+ clinics and over 600 service lines with an omnichannel presence across 26 cities and 15 states. During FY26 it continued to strengthen the clinic network through new clinic launches, strategic relocations and infrastructure upgrades aimed at enhancing accessibility, convenience and customer experience, and it expanded and upgraded the network alongside the introduction of advanced technologies and innovative products. Management states it accelerated investments during the year in advanced dermatology platforms, diagnostics, digital engagement, clinic infrastructure, and innovation-led products and services, together with technology integration, network enhancement, branding and capability-building initiatives, describing these as building the foundation for sustainable long-term growth. The product footprint was also widened, with 75+ product offerings in FY26. On the funding side, the Company issued 20,90,068 equity shares on August 12, 2025 to Axana Estates LLP pursuant to a preferential issue. No rupee capex outlay, commissioning schedule, clinic-addition target or dated expansion project is disclosed in the routed sections.

risks.note: Explicitly tracked by management as a key external risk factor. Kaya's demand is discretionary, consumer-led aesthetic care, and the MD&A itself describes rapidly changing consumer mindsets - the move to preventive and personalised regimes, premiumisation and digital-led discovery - so a change in consumer preference directly affects clinic footfall and treatment mix.

Explicitly tracked by management. The MD&A notes the industry is transitioning to a more organised, technology-driven and experience-led ecosystem in which differentiation will be driven by clinical credibility, innovation and customer engagement, and that players integrating advanced technologies with personalised care and strong brand positioning are likely to capture disproportionate value - implying share loss risk for those who do not.

Explicitly tracked by management. Treatment outcomes in aesthetic dermatology depend on device and protocol technology (laser platforms, energy-based devices, regenerative and diagnostic systems); continuous technology refresh is required to stay competitive, making the business exposed to obsolescence of installed clinical platforms.

Explicitly tracked by management, with the risk framework designed to ensure alignment with evolving regulatory requirements. Kaya operates medically supervised clinical procedures and sells dermatology-linked products, both of which sit in regulated territory.

risks.risk: Dependence on continuous clinical innovation and protocol adoption to sustain positioning
risks.note: Management states the Company aims to scale leadership by continuously enhancing service offerings and strengthening technology capabilities; its stated competitive position rests on advanced technology adoption (for example Aerolase, MCT and Artiqa platforms) and standardised protocols, so a lag in adoption would erode the differentiation the strategy relies on.
